sections.title: Test Coverage Analysis
sections.content: **Top-line finding: 0% coverage.** There is no `package.json`, no `jest`/`mocha`/`vitest` config, and no `bats`/shell test harness anywhere in the repo. Every function below is currently untested.

sections.title: 1. `router.js` — keyword-based agent router (`.claude/helpers/router.js:47-91`)
2. `memory.js` — key/value store (`.claude/helpers/memory.js:13-83`)
3. `session.js` — session lifecycle (`.claude/helpers/session.js:21-157`)
4. `github-safe.js` — injection-safe `gh` wrapper (`.claude/helpers/github-safe.js`)
5. `hook-handler.cjs` — hook dispatcher (`.claude/helpers/hook-handler.cjs`)
6. `scripts/claude-resume.sh` — project ID derivation & session commands
sections.content:
Untested: the `CLAUDE_PROJECT_ID` transform (`scripts/claude-resume.sh:38`), `cmd_resume_id`, `cmd_fork`, `cmd_from_pr`, `cmd_cleanup`, `cmd_export`.

Gaps:
- Project-ID path transform (`/` → `-`, leading slash collapse) is exactly the kind of stringly-typed logic that silently breaks — e.g. a workspace path containing a literal `-` already, or a trailing slash, changes the derived ID with no test locking in the expected mapping (this is also documented as load-bearing in `CLAUDE.md`).
- `cmd_from_pr` behavior when given a nonexistent PR number.
- `cmd_cleanup`/`cmd_export` are destructive/exporting operations with no test verifying they don't delete non-stale entries or leak data.
- No test that `check_claude`/`check_ruflo` degrade gracefully (hooks are documented as fail-silent via `|| true`) when those binaries are absent from `PATH`.

sections.title: tests/claude-resume.bats  (requires bats-core; run: bats tests/claude-resume.bats)
Integration test gaps (highest-impact, currently zero coverage)
sections.content:
1. **Full hook lifecycle**: `session-restore` → several `pre-edit`/`post-edit` → `session-end` — no test exercises this sequence against real files in a scratch dir, so regressions like #2307 (the race this repo's own comments reference) would ship silently.
2. **`claude-resume.sh` ↔ `session.js` ↔ memory layer consistency**: the 3-layer memory system (Claude Code memory, AgentDB, ruflo session state) described in `CLAUDE.md` has no test asserting all three actually agree after a resume/fork/end cycle.
3. **`hook-handler.cjs` → `router.js`/`intelligence.cjs` wiring**: `safeRequire`'s console-suppression trick means a broken helper module fails silently — no smoke test asserts `route` output for a known prompt actually reaches stdout unmangled.
4. **Cross-platform stdin handling** in `readStdin()` — repo explicitly calls out Windows hangs as the reason for the 500ms timeout; no test simulates a stdin stream that never closes.

sections.title: Suggested setup
sections.content:
No test runner is configured anywhere. Given the repo intentionally avoids a `package.json` (per its own CLAUDE.md, this is tooling/config, not an app), the lowest-friction option is Node's built-in `node:test` (zero dependencies, `node --test test/`) for the `.js`/`.cjs`/`.mjs` helpers, and `bats-core` for `scripts/claude-resume.sh`. Both can run without adding a `package.json` — `node --test` works standalone, and `bats` is invoked directly.

**Not evaluated**: `intelligence.cjs` (1,058 lines), `statusline.cjs`/`statusline.js` (1,056 lines combined), `metrics-db.mjs` (503 lines), and `auto-memory-hook.mjs` (430 lines) — these are the largest untested files in the repo but weren't deep-read here; they warrant the same treatment as a follow-up given their size.
